links_against.note: Every technosphere exchange names the BAFU-2026 code of its supplier; every elementary flow names its code AND the database it came from. The importer resolves those codes in the target project and refuses to write anything if one is missing.

strategies.S2: a unit process of the same product exists in BAFU - its structure reused, amounts calibrated

strategies.S4: nothing but the aggregated vector - never used on its own
strategies.S5: hybrid: the explicit exchanges plus a residual block, so the rebuild reproduces the original exactly

replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: transcription drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: per 1 m3 of wood wool boards, cement bonded; the product row reads 'wood wool boards, cement bonded, at plant  1.00E+00 m3' (medium density 450 kg/m3, range 360-570 kg/m3); allocation: none stated for the board process itself. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI wood as fuel and const. mat. - Werner.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 1f2e06f8a69ca03e…, text sha256 e4722b9d949de48a…

gaps_reported_by_model: Electricity and light-fuel-oil heat are printed as 'confidential'; their amounts come from the calibration step, not from the report. The bounds used (1-500 kWh, 1-5000 MJ per m3) are wide search ranges chosen here, not report values.
No process emissions are documented ('No process emission data are available' in the BAFU metadata); only the calculated waste heat.
The excerpt gives no packaging, no water emissions and no solid waste for the board process.

datasets.bafu_name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant

replaces.name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: transcription drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: per 1 kg of TiO2; Tab. 85.3 is headed 'Kg per kg of product', Tab. 85.5 'Consumption per kg of product (MJ/kg)', Tab. 85.7 and Tab. 85.9 'Gram per kg of product'. The CHLORIDE-process column is used.; allocation: none stated for the TiO2 process itself. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 68e0839ffea919f9…, text sha256 e1b3f9c29c3269b8…

gaps_reported_by_model: Section 85.6 says 'This inventory is based on confidential information provided by industry sources. The input information may not be divulged.' The printed BAT-Notes figures are what the report compares against, not necessarily the exact dataset amounts.
No transport, no infrastructure (chemical plant) and no water input are quantified anywhere in the excerpt for the TiO2 process; they are therefore not included.
Tab. 85.5 gives no coal for the chloride process and no breakdown of which fuel produces the steam beyond the sentence about a natural gas boiler.
The excerpt gives no process water, no NOx and no organic emissions for the chloride route.
skipped_items: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant: product — Reference product; the whole excerpt is per kg of product.

nodes.name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.reference_product: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant, disaggregated
nodes.comment: drafted from 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf pp. 845-847

technosphere.comment: Chloride-process precursor. The text adds 'The chloride process titanium dioxide is also assumed to stem from ilmenite, although in fact rutile, synthetic rutile and /or beneficiate are used. The data for mining of ilmenite are taken from (BUWAL 232).' so the supplying dataset is the ilmenite/rutile ore, not TiO2 itself.

provenance.quote: Synthetic rutile   ng   1.06   (Chemlink.com)   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, chloride-process column, 'Kg per kg of product']
provenance.mapping_reason: Tab. 85.3 names 'Synthetic rutile' for the chloride route; the rutile concentrate is that material, while ilmenite is the lower-grade ore the sulfate route uses.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Chlorine, liquid, production mix, at plant
technosphere.comment: Printed value for the chloride process.
technosphere.supplier_name: Chlorine, liquid, production mix, at plant

provenance.quote: Chlorine   na   0.18   (UBA BAT Notes, 2001)   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, chloride-process column]
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and a production mix, as the report gives no specific electrolysis route; chlorine dioxide is a different chemical.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid
technosphere.comment: 1.51 MJ (TiO2 manufacture) + 0.83 MJ (follow-up treatment) = 2.34 MJ/kg, the two columns of the same row. The text says the model facility 'imports UCTE grid electricity'.
technosphere.supplier_name: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid

provenance.quote: Electric energy   1.51   0.83   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process), TiO2 manufacture + Follow-up treatment]
provenance.factor_source: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ, so MJ x 0.2778 = kWh (ecoinvent convention)
provenance.mapping_reason: The report says the model plant 'imports UCTE grid electricity'; this is the UCTE production mix, beating the single-fuel UCTE variants and the RER/CH grids.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW
technosphere.comment: 1.7 + 7.7 = 9.4 MJ/kg. The text: 'The model facility portrayed here uses natural gas in a boiler to produce steam', so the steam is entered as natural-gas heat in MJ.
technosphere.supplier_name: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW

provenance.quote: Steam   1.7   7.7   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.mapping_reason: The report: 'uses natural gas in a boiler to produce steam'; this is delivered heat in MJ from a natural-gas furnace, which matches the MJ/kg the table gives, beating the 'burned in' variants that model the combustion itself.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW
technosphere.comment: 2.9 + 4.2 = 7.1 MJ/kg of direct process gas, separate from the gas burned for steam.
technosphere.supplier_name: Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW

provenance.quote: Gas   2.9   4.2   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.mapping_reason: Direct process gas burned on site, which is what the separate 'Gas' row of Tab. 85.5 is, as opposed to the gas that makes the steam.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill
technosphere.comment: 0.11 + 2.25 = 2.36 g/kg. Treated here as a disposal service (an input), since the report lists it under wastewater emissions but it is a solid residue. Low confidence on which disposal dataset applies.
technosphere.supplier_name: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill

provenance.quote: Filter residues   0.11   2.25   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The disposal dataset made for exactly this residue stream of the chloride route, beating the SO4 variant and the generic residue landfills.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill
technosphere.comment: The excerpt gives 184 g/kg from the BAT notes and says industry suggests up to 1 kg/kg; entered as a bounded free input over exactly that printed range.
technosphere.supplier_name: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill

provenance.quote: Chloride process. According to (UBA BAT Notes, 2001), chloride process sludges total 184 g / kg product. Industry sources however suggest somewhat higher values, ranging up to 1 kg / kg product
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Same stream as the filter residues and the only chloride-route TiO2 disposal dataset in the database.

biosphere.comment: 0.005 g (storage) + 0.186 g (follow-up treatment) = 0.191 g/kg. The report does not state a size fraction for the chloride route.

provenance.quote: Particles   0.005   ng   ng   0.186   [Tab. 85.7 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The only candidate; the report states no particle size fraction for TiO2, so the unspecified particulate flow is the honest choice.

biosphere.comment: The asterisk in the table marks 0.024 g/kg as the value the report actually uses for the model chloride plant.

provenance.quote: HCl   ng   0.007   0.024 *   ng   * This value is used for the model chloride plant.   [Tab. 85.7]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance in the stated air compartment; the soil and water copies are the wrong compartment and 'Chloride' is the ion, not HCl.

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: SO2   ng   ng   1.68   ng   [Tab. 85.7 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process), off-gas treatment]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; 'Sulfur Oxides' is the aggregate and 'Sulfur' the element.

biosphere.comment: The table prints 0.011 g/kg but the footnote below it states 'This report uses a value of 0.5 g iron per kg produced TiO2'; the footnote value is the one the dataset was built with.

provenance.quote: Iron   0.011 *   ng   ...   This report uses a value of 0.5 g iron per kg produced TiO2   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The report says only 'Iron' with no oxidation state, so the unspecified iron flow beats Iron(2+) and Iron(3+).

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: Cadmium   0.00000022   ng   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; Cadmium(2+) presumes an oxidation state the report does not give and Cadmium-109 is a radionuclide.

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: Mercury   0.00000022   ng   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; Mercury(2+) presumes a speciation the report does not give.

strategy.label: transcription drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: per 1 kg of wood preservative; the table's product row reads 'wood preservative, inorganic salt, containing Cr, at plant  1.00E+00 kg'; allocation: none stated; single-product process. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI wood as fuel and const. mat. - Werner.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 1f2e06f8a69ca03e…, text sha256 207d840fb9d1bcd4…

gaps_reported_by_model: The five material amounts (boric acid, chromium oxide, copper oxide, UCTE electricity, tap water) are printed as 'confidential'. The excerpt gives no numbers for them at all; they are entered as free parameters with wide bounds and are determined by the calibration step, not by the report.
The report gives no process emissions for this dataset ('No process emission data are available' in the BAFU metadata); only the calculated waste heat is listed.

The bounds attached to the confidential rows are not from the report. They are deliberately wide search ranges (0.001-1 kg for the salts, since the product is 1 kg of mixed salts; 1e-4 to 5 kWh; 0.001-100 kg of water).

replaces.name: Anthraquinone, at plant
replaces.note: the aggregated ('system terminated') BAFU-2026 dataset this unit process rebuilds

strategy.label: transcription drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: the chromic acid column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000' - i.e. per 3000 kg of anthraquinone; allocation: none stated. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

evidence.source: 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf
evidence.note: report sha256 68e0839ffea919f9…, text sha256 6d1899c288e051fa…

gaps_reported_by_model: The dataset is an 80/20 average: 'an average process from the chromic acid process in Tab. 44.3 and the information at EMPA from the former studies is established - with an amount of 80% chromic acid process'. Only the chromic acid column is printed; 'the respective information from EMPA is not shown here due to confidentiality reasons'. The extracted list is therefore the 80 % share only.

The EMPA share contributes chlorobenzene (modelled as benzene + chlorine at 95 % yield) and aluminium chloride (modelled as aluminium + chlorine at 95 % yield). No amounts are given, so those four inputs are NOT included here.
The sulphuric acid amount actually used is 'the stoechiometric value based on an efficiency of 95%', which the report does not print.
Electricity, steam, infrastructure and both transports are named by the report but carry no numbers; they are free parameters for calibration.
The air emissions are given as percentage rules applied to inputs the report itself replaces, so their absolute values are uncertain.
'Due to confidentiality reasons, only the cumulated data from this dataset are available for the user of ...' - the dataset's own unit-process table is not published.
skipped_items: air (flow rate): ignore — Explicitly excluded by the report: 'The amount of air consumed is not shown in the ecoinvent dataset according to Frischknecht et al. (2007).' It is also a flow rate, not an amount per batch.

Sulphuric acid to air: no flow chosen (No candidate is airborne sulphuric acid or a sulfate aerosol. Sulfur Dioxide would be a different substance with a different formation route, and mapping sulphuric acid mist onto SO2 would be a substitution the report does not make. Reported as missing instead.)

naphthalene: ignore — Belongs to the naphthalene route, marked only with 'x' (no quantity). The report says 'this second source allows no quantification of the process in three of the four cases' and builds the dataset from the chromic acid column only.
xylene: ignore — Unquantified column of a route not used for this dataset.
butadiene: ignore — Unquantified column of a route not used for this dataset.
anthraquinone: product — Reference product; fixes the basis at 3000 kg.

technosphere.comment: Printed value. The report does not say which water dataset is meant; low confidence on the mapping, not on the number.

provenance.quote: water   kg   9000   [Tab. 44.3 Input and output data for the production of anthraquinone, chromic acid column]
provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
provenance.mapping_reason: Process water for a chemical synthesis; decarbonised water is the standard ecoinvent chemical-process water, less treated (and so less committal) than completely softened or deionised water.

technosphere.comment: Printed value. The report maps it itself: 'the amount of anthracene used for the production of anthrachinone is shown in this study here as "chemiacal organics, unspecified"' because anthracene is not in ecoinvent.

provenance.quote: anthracene   kg   2600   [Tab. 44.3, chromic acid column]
provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
provenance.mapping_reason: The report itself states the anthracene input 'is shown in this study here as "chemiacal organics, unspecified"' because anthracene is not in the database; this is that proxy dataset.

technosphere.comment: The report explicitly rejects this number: 'As then the above listed amount of sulphuric acid is not sufficient for the process equation, instead the stoechiometric value based on an efficiency of 95% is used here.' The stoichiometric value is not printed, so this is a bounded free input: raw_min is the printed 48 % active substance (4896 kg/3000 kg) and raw_max is a wide upper search bound chosen here, NOT a report value.

provenance.quote: sulphuric acid, 48%   kg   10200   [Tab. 44.3, chromic acid column]
provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
provenance.factor_source: the row is headed 'sulphuric acid, 48%' and the text says 'The input of sulphuric acid and of sodium dichromate is expressed as amount of active substance only', so x0.48 gives the active substance
provenance.mapping_reason: Purchased sulphuric acid at RER; the viscose by-product acid is a different source the report does not mention.

technosphere.comment: Printed value, converted to active substance as the report states.

provenance.quote: sodium dichromate, 20%   kg   23500   [Tab. 44.3, chromic acid column]
provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
provenance.factor_source: the row is headed 'sodium dichromate, 20%' and the text says the input 'is expressed as amount of active substance only', so x0.20 gives the active substance
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance; every other candidate is a different sodium salt.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid
technosphere.comment: The input is named by the report but no amount is given for the chromic acid process ('In case of the chromic acid process no information about energy production is given. Therefore, it is assumed that the energy consumption is similar like in the other dataset.'). Entered as a free parameter with a wide search range; raw_value is a seed, not a report number.
technosphere.supplier_name: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid

provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
provenance.mapping_reason: The report names 'electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid'; this candidate is that exact dataset at UCTE, beating the RER/CH grid mixes and the single-fuel UCTE variants.

provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
provenance.mapping_reason: The only candidate and the exact dataset the report names.

technosphere.comment: Named by the report, no amount given. Free parameter; raw_value is a seed, not a report number.

provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
provenance.mapping_reason: The exact infrastructure module the report names.

provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
provenance.mapping_reason: The report names 'transport, freight, rail' without a traction specification, which is exactly this RER average; the electricity-only and CH shunting variants are narrower.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Transport, freight, lorry, 16t-32t gross weight, fleet average

technosphere.supplier_name: Transport, freight, lorry, 16t-32t gross weight, fleet average

provenance.quote: Infrastructure and Transport: ... standard distances according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used within this dataset.
provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
provenance.mapping_reason: The report names 'transport, lorry >16t, fleet average'; the 16t-32t RER fleet average is that dataset at the process's own location, beating the CH copy and the other weight classes.

biosphere.comment: Printed per kg of product. Mapped to sulfate in water, the EF 3.1 flow that carries dissolved sulphuric acid.

provenance.quote: No removal efficiency for sulphuric acid was assumed, leading to emissions of 220 g sulphuric acid per kg product in the treated water.
provenance.per: per kg anthraquinone (value printed per kg product in the text of 44.4.1)
provenance.factor_source: g -> kg (x0.001) and then the table basis is 3000 kg of product while this value is printed 'per kg product'; x3000 puts it on the same basis (x3000): net factor 3.0
provenance.mapping_reason: Sulphuric acid released into treated wastewater is dissociated sulfate; the EF 3.1 sulfate ion in water is the closest available flow, and no undissociated sulphuric-acid water flow exists in the candidate list.

biosphere.comment: Printed per kg of product.

provenance.quote: The remaining amount of sodium dichromate is approximated by an emission of about 1 mol of sodium, e.g. 23 g/kg
provenance.per: per kg anthraquinone (value printed per kg product in the text of 44.4.1)
provenance.factor_source: g -> kg (x0.001) and then the table basis is 3000 kg of product while this value is printed 'per kg product'; x3000 puts it on the same basis (x3000): net factor 3.0
provenance.mapping_reason: The report says '1 mol of sodium' released in treated water, i.e. the dissolved ion; Sodium-24 is a radionuclide.

biosphere.comment: Printed per kg of product. The report does not say whether this is Cr(III) or Cr(VI).

provenance.quote: and of 0.5 mol (due to a removal efficiency of 50%) of chromium ions, e.g. of 26 g/kg.
provenance.per: per kg anthraquinone (value printed per kg product in the text of 44.4.1)
provenance.factor_source: g -> kg (x0.001) and then the table basis is 3000 kg of product while this value is printed 'per kg product'; x3000 puts it on the same basis (x3000): net factor 3.0
provenance.mapping_reason: The report says 'chromium ions' without giving the oxidation state, so the unspecified chromium flow to water is correct; Chromium VI would assert a speciation the report does not state.

biosphere.comment: Rule-derived, not printed as a number. Mapped to chromium VI because sodium dichromate is a Cr(VI) salt; low confidence on that mapping.

provenance.quote: and 0.2% of the sodium dichromate input (assumption);
provenance.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
provenance.factor_source: 0.2 % of the sodium dichromate input (report rule) x 0.20 active substance (row header 'sodium dichromate, 20%'): 0.002 x 0.20 = 0.0004
provenance.mapping_reason: Sodium dichromate is a Cr(VI) salt and the report's air emission is that dust; Chromium(6+) to air is the matching speciated flow, while plain 'Chromium' to air would lose the hexavalent state the substance actually has.

gaps_reported_by_model: Section 85.6: 'This inventory is based on confidential information provided by industry sources. The input information may not be divulged.' The BAT-Notes tables are what the report prints; the dataset's exact amounts are not published.
No transport, no chemical-plant infrastructure and no process-water input are quantified in the excerpt.
The report mentions that gypsum can be generated if the acid is neutralised with lime and that filter salts can be sold, but gives no amounts and no allocation, so neither is included.
Several air-emission rows (NOx, H2S) are printed only as ranges with no value marked as used; their midpoints are used and flagged low confidence.

technosphere.comment: Printed as a range 2.4-3.5 kg/kg; entered as a bounded free input over exactly that range, raw_value is its midpoint.

provenance.quote: Sulphuric acid   2.4 – 3.5   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, sulfate-process column, 'Kg per kg of product']
provenance.mapping_reason: Purchased sulphuric acid at RER; the viscose-production by-product acid is a different, allocated source the report does not mention.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xx Ilmenite, 54% titanium dioxide, at plant
technosphere.comment: 'Ca. 2' kg/kg. The text: 'This report assumes that the sulfate process titanium dioxide has been manufactured from ilmenite ... The data for mining of ilmenite are taken from (BUWAL 232).'
technosphere.supplier_name: xx Ilmenite, 54% titanium dioxide, at plant

provenance.quote: Rutile, ilmenite   Ca. 2   na   Industry sources   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, sulfate-process column]
provenance.mapping_reason: The report states 'the sulfate process titanium dioxide has been manufactured from ilmenite'; the ilmenite dataset therefore beats the higher-grade rutile concentrate.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid
technosphere.comment: Three column ranges on one row; min = 1.5+0.6+0.13 = 2.23 MJ, max = 2.31+1.46+1.3 = 5.07 MJ, raw_value is the midpoint. Entered as a bounded free input. The text says power and steam come from a CHP plant plus UCTE grid electricity.
technosphere.supplier_name: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid

provenance.quote: Electric energy   1.5 – 2.31   0.6 – 1.46   0.13-1.3   [Tab. 85.4 energy consumption for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.factor_source: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ, so MJ x 0.2778 = kWh (ecoinvent convention)
provenance.mapping_reason: The report says the plant uses 'electricity from the UCTE grid'; this is the UCTE production mix.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW
technosphere.comment: min = 3.7+6.7+0 = 10.4 MJ, max = 7.7+10.47+6.07 = 24.24 MJ. The text: 'Both steam and electricity can be generated from combined heat and power plants ... Steam can stem from sulphuric acid plants'. Entered as generic industrial heat over the printed range.
technosphere.supplier_name: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW

provenance.quote: Steam   3.7 – 7.7   6.7 – 10.47   0 – 6.07   [Tab. 85.4 energy consumption for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.mapping_reason: Delivered heat in MJ, matching the MJ/kg basis of Tab. 85.4; the report says steam comes from a CHP plant or a sulphuric acid plant but gives no dataset, so generic industrial heat is the least-committal fit.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW
technosphere.supplier_name: Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW

provenance.quote: Gas   7.3 – 11.85   2.37 – 4.22   0 – 0.1   [Tab. 85.4 energy consumption for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.mapping_reason: The separate 'Gas' row is gas burned on site, as opposed to the gas that makes the steam.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: Hard coal, burned in industrial furnace 1-10MW
technosphere.comment: Only the acid-concentration / filter-salt-decomposition step uses coal, 5.8-8.5 MJ/kg.
technosphere.supplier_name: Hard coal, burned in industrial furnace 1-10MW

provenance.quote: Coal   na   na   5.8 – 8.5   [Tab. 85.4 energy consumption for TiO2 production (sulfate process), acid concentration and filter salt decomposition column]
provenance.mapping_reason: Coal burned on site in MJ; the 'Heat, at hard coal industrial furnace' variant is the delivered-heat form of the same process and either fits, but the combustion dataset is the direct reading of a fuel row.

technosphere.supplier_name_in_spec: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. SO4, 30% water, to residual material landfill
technosphere.comment: Section 85.6.6 states the value the report assumes (480 g/kg). Low confidence only on which disposal dataset matches 'solidified in cement and landfilled'.
technosphere.supplier_name: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. SO4, 30% water, to residual material landfill

provenance.quote: Sulfate process: According to (UBA BAT Notes, 2001), residues generated from ore digestion total 340 – 670 g / kg product. These wastes are disposal of as hazardous wastes. ... This report assumes that 480 g / kg product are produced, solidified in cement and landfilled.
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The disposal dataset made for exactly this residue stream of the sulfate route, beating the Cl variant and the generic residue landfills.

biosphere.comment: The footnote fixes the calcination column at '0.7 g / kg is used in this report'. The report states no particle size fraction for TiO2, so the unspecified particulate flow is used.

provenance.quote: Particles   0.001 – 0.04   ng   0.13-1.3 *   0.002 – 0.12   * 0.7 g / kg is used in this report   [Tab. 85.6 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The report states no size fraction for TiO2 dust, so the unspecified particulate flow beats assuming PM2.5.

biosphere.comment: Printed only as ranges with no value marked as used; raw_value is the midpoint of the calcination range. Low confidence.

provenance.quote: NOx   0.001 – 0.043   ng   0 – 6.07   [Tab. 85.6 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: 'NOx' is the aggregate nitrogen oxides flow, not nitrogen dioxide alone.

biosphere.comment: The calcination column prints 1 g/kg carrying the footnote marker that reads 'This value is used for the model sulfate plant'.

provenance.quote: SO2   ng   0 – 0.119   1*   ng   ** This value is used for the model sulfate plant.   [Tab. 85.6 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; 'Sulfur Oxides' is the aggregate.

biosphere.comment: Range 0-0.005 g/kg, no value marked as used; raw_value is the midpoint.

provenance.quote: H2S   ng   0 – 0.005   ng   ng   [Tab. 85.6 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance in the stated air compartment.

biosphere.comment: The footnote fixes the filtration/washing column at 150 g/kg. Section 85.6.5 additionally assumes 'roughly 50 g sulfate / kg product' from the spent acid, which is listed as a separate item.

provenance.quote: Sulfate   30 – 300 *   80 - 110   * This report uses a value of 150 g sulfate per kg produced TiO2   [Tab. 85.8 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Dissolved sulfate in wastewater; the EF 3.1 sulfate ion in the water compartment, beating the named metal sulfates and the residual-database long-term groundwater flow.

biosphere.comment: Section 85.6.5 'Liquid wastes'. It is not clear whether this 50 g/kg is additional to the 150 g/kg of Tab. 85.8 or part of it; both are listed so the reviewer can decide.

provenance.quote: According to (UBA BAT Notes, 2001) Figure 2.1.3.1, sulphuric acid that enters the wastewater from the sulfate process contains 30 – 300 g sulfate per kg spent acid (see Tab. 85.9). An average of roughly 50 g sulfate / kg product.is assumed in this report.
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Same substance and compartment as the Tab. 85.8 sulfate row.

biosphere.comment: Footnote fixes the value at 2 g/kg.

provenance.quote: Iron   0.25 – 5 **   ng   ** This report uses a value of 2 g iron per kg produced TiO2   [Tab. 85.8 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: The report gives no oxidation state, so the unspecified iron flow is correct.

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: Cadmium   0.000001   ng   [Tab. 85.8 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment.

biosphere.comment: Printed value.

provenance.quote: Mercury   0.00000032   ng   [Tab. 85.8 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
provenance.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
provenance.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment.

strategy.label: structural model: the rebuilt 'at plant' node plus distribution transport, distances calibrated

strategy.label: template transfer from the CH unit process of the same product, main amounts calibrated within 0.5-2x
strategy.note: The DE board inventory sits in a confidential annex of the KBOB 2016 report, so the structure of BAFU's own CH unit process (10 inputs) is reused, scaled to 10 kg/m2, with the grid switched to DE. Six main amounts are fitted within bounds; three land on the 2x ceiling, i.e. the German plant is more energy-intensive than the template allows. S5 hybrid built on top.

evidence.source: bafu-2026: Gypsum fibre board, at plant [CH] (unit process, 10 inputs)
evidence.note: Same product, Swiss unit process. The DE dataset (treeze/QualiBOB 2016, 'data from German manufacturers') keeps its board-production inventory in a confidential annex, so the CH structure is reused; grid electricity switched to DE; the six main amounts may move within 0.25-4x of the CH value. The DE dataset is per m2; the CH template (per kg) is scaled by 10 kg/m2 (Kasser 2016, D: 10 kg/m2, 12.5 mm). Free amounts bounded to 0.5-2x the scaled template.

evidence.source: 2016 - Renewal and expansion of LCA data in KBOB - Kasser.pdf
evidence.note: 10 kg/m2, 12.5 mm; board inventory confidential (Anhang Z); binder and transport inventories printed.
